Winding number of each input feature in every triangle

Source: R/cdt.R
cdt_winding.Rd

For a triangulation of several overlapping inputs, find which inputs cover each triangle. Triangles are walked from a starting point known to be covered by nothing. Stepping across an ordinary edge changes nothing; stepping across a fixed edge changes the winding number of each feature covering it by plus or minus one, according to the direction of its input segment (see edge_sources in cdt_triangulate()). Only the mesh is used, with no point-in-polygon test.

Usage

cdt_winding(x, owner, outside, n_features = max(owner))

Arguments

x

a result of cdt_triangulate() made with edge_sources = TRUE

owner

the feature of each input segment, an integer vector with one element for each segment passed as s0, s1. Zero means the segment is not counted, for a frame or any other construction line. Features are 1 to n_features.

outside

a point c(x, y) in the mesh, covered by no feature

n_features

the number of features, by default the largest in owner

Value

an integer matrix with one row per triangle (the rows of x$T) and one column per feature, giving its winding number there. Triangles the walk cannot reach are NA, with a warning.

Details

Outer rings should run counter-clockwise and holes clockwise, which makes the winding number 1 inside the feature (a clockwise outer ring gives -1). Overlapping and shared edges are handled, and refinement does not matter, as edge_sources follows each input through splits.

The mesh needs a region covered by nothing to start from, for example a frame around the inputs (give it feature 0, or a feature that you ignore), and the walk must be able to reach every triangle. Use erase = "hull", or the default "outer" with a frame. With erase = "holes" the triangles are not connected through the erased regions, so some are not reached.

Examples

## two overlapping squares, in a frame (feature 0)
sq <- function(x0, y0, x1, y1) rbind(c(x0, y0), c(x1, y0), c(x1, y1), c(x0, y1))
rings <- list(sq(0, 0, 2, 2), sq(1, 1, 3, 3), sq(-1, -1, 4, 4))
feature <- c(1, 2, 0)
n <- vapply(rings, nrow, 1L)
first <- cumsum(c(0L, n[-length(n)]))
xy <- do.call(rbind, rings)
s0 <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(n), function(k) first[k] + 1:4))
s1 <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(n), function(k) first[k] + c(2:4, 1L)))
r <- cdt_triangulate(xy[, 1], xy[, 2], s0, s1, max_area = 0.5,
                     edge_sources = TRUE)
w <- cdt_winding(r, owner = rep(feature, n), outside = c(-0.5, -0.5))
## triangles by the features covering them
table(feature_1 = w[, 1], feature_2 = w[, 2])
#>          feature_2
#> feature_1  0  1
#>         0 48  6
#>         1  6  2
